title: Aetolian League
capsule: The Aetolian League was a federal confederacy of Greek communities centered in Aetolia in western Greece, which rose to prominence after its forces helped repel the Galatian invasion at Delphi in 279 BC and subsequently controlled the Amphictyonic sanctuary and much of central Greece. The League aligned with Rome against Philip V in the First Macedonian War and aided the Roman victory at Cynoscephalae in 197 BC, but then invited Antiochus III of Syria against Rome in 192 BC, overreaching catastrophically. After Antiochus was defeated at Magnesia in 190 BC the Romans besieged Ambracia, and the Peace of Ambracia of 188 BC compelled the League to acknowledge Roman supremacy and surrender most of its territorial acquisitions, reducing it to a client state.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The League's political history is well attested in Polybius, Livy, and Delphic epigraphy; precise boundaries of member communities shifted frequently and are imperfectly reconstructed from ancient sources.
